# Consent to Ecclesiastical Jurisdiction and Agreement to Arbitrate

## When to use this

This is the instrument on which the Kingdom's judicial power actually rests. Not
the Charter, which binds nobody who did not accept it, and not the tribunal's own
rules — individual signatures, one at a time, taken before anything has gone
wrong.

Put it in front of every member on admission, every officer on commission, every
employee on hire, and every contractor and volunteer whose work could produce a
dispute. Take it while relations are warm and nothing is contested. An agreement
signed in a calm month is worth everything; the same words offered after a
grievance has formed are worth almost nothing, because a person who is already in
a fight will decline, and if they sign anyway a court will read the document
narrowly and look hard at how it was obtained.

Do not use it as a condition of pastoral care, of attendance at worship, of
receiving charitable assistance, or of a child's participation in anything. An
agreement extracted from someone who needed something the Kingdom was holding is
the paradigm case of the agreement that fails — and it fails in a way that
contaminates every other agreement executed on the same form.

Two distinct things are being signed here and the template keeps them apart on
purpose. Article 1 is consent to the Kingdom's internal religious governance,
which civil courts largely will not review but also will not enforce. Article 2 is
an agreement to arbitrate, which is the only mechanism by which a determination of
the Kingdom's tribunal becomes something a civil court will confirm and enforce.
A signer may be given both or, where appropriate, only the first.

## Before you send

- [ ] **Nothing is in dispute between the Kingdom and this person,** and none is
      reasonably anticipated. Record that fact. A post-dispute submission is a
      different and much narrower instrument.
- [ ] **The signer is eighteen or over.** A minor's contract is voidable by them
      and may be disaffirmed within a reasonable time after majority, and a
      parent generally cannot waive a child's own claims. Do not build anything
      on a minor's signature.
- [ ] **The signer is given the document to keep, in advance,** with at least
      [seven] days to consider it before any signature is asked for. Record the
      date it was handed over as well as the date it was signed. A same-day
      signature on a document first seen that morning is a fact an adversary will
      make much of.
- [ ] **The written advice to consult a lawyer is in the document, above the
      signature line,** and was also given orally. Record which.
- [ ] **Declining carries no penalty, and the signer is told so in writing** —
      no loss of membership, office, employment, assistance, standing, or
      participation. This must be true in fact as well as on the page.
- [ ] **The scope clause has been read against this signer's actual role.** An
      arbitration clause that reaches disputes this person could never have is
      overbreadth a court will notice; one that omits the disputes they realistically
      could have is a clause that will not be there when it is needed.
- [ ] **The rules named in Article 4 exist, are in force, are the version
      attached, and the signer receives a copy.** An agreement pointing at rules
      that cannot be produced invites the argument that the parties never agreed
      on a process at all.
- [ ] **The Kingdom will in fact pay the forum's costs** as Article 7 states.
- [ ] **No clause purports to waive anything unwaivable.** Criminal jurisdiction,
      mandated reporting under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 17a-101 et seq., child
      protection, the right to file a charge with a government agency, sexual
      assault and sexual harassment claims under 9 U.S.C. §§ 401–402. If a
      clause of this kind has crept into any version in circulation, do not
      reinterpret it — re-execute a clean instrument.
- [ ] **The execution is witnessed and notarised.** Neither is required for
      validity; both make a later denial of signature very hard to sustain, and a
      denial of signature is what actually happens when arbitration is resisted.
- [ ] **A signed original is delivered to the signer** and the date of delivery
      recorded.
- [ ] **A record is opened in the Register of Consents to Jurisdiction and
      Arbitration** with the wet-ink original's physical location entered, and
      the original is stored somewhere other than the building holding the only
      copy.

## The instrument

```
APEX KINGDOM

CONSENT TO ECCLESIASTICAL JURISDICTION
AND AGREEMENT TO ARBITRATE

Instrument reference: [CONS RECORD NUMBER]
Form and version: [TITLE, rev. [N] ([YYYY-MM])]


-----------------------------------------------------------------------
PLEASE READ THIS FIRST — A PLAIN-LANGUAGE SUMMARY

This box summarises the agreement. It is not the agreement itself; the
numbered articles below are. If the two ever differ, the articles govern.

1.  You are agreeing that certain disputes between you and Apex Kingdom
    will be decided by religious arbitration instead of by a court.

2.  That means you are giving up your right to have those disputes
    decided by a judge or a jury, and giving up the right to appeal in
    the ordinary way. An arbitration decision is final, and a court will
    normally enforce it without re-examining who was right.

3.  It covers disputes about your membership, your office, your role, the
    Kingdom's internal governance and discipline, and the agreements
    listed in Article 2. It does not cover everything.

4.  It does NOT cover, and cannot cover: any criminal matter; anything to
    do with the safety or protection of a child; your duty or your right
    to report suspected abuse or neglect to the State of Connecticut or
    to the police; your right to file a complaint with a government
    agency; any claim of sexual assault or sexual harassment, which you
    may take to court regardless of this agreement; and any other right
    the law says cannot be given up by agreement.

5.  You do not have to sign this. If you decline, nothing happens to you.
    You remain a member in full standing with every right you now have,
    and the Kingdom will not treat you differently for declining. You may
    take this document to a lawyer of your own choosing, at your own
    expense, before you sign, and you are encouraged to do so.

6.  The Kingdom pays the arbitrators' fees and the costs of the forum.
    You pay for your own lawyer if you choose to have one.

7.  You have at least [SEVEN] days to think about this. Take them.

8.  You will be given a signed copy to keep.

9.  You may withdraw from this agreement at any time by written notice.
    Withdrawal takes effect going forward; a dispute already submitted
    to arbitration before your notice stays there.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------


THIS AGREEMENT is made on [DATE]

BETWEEN:

  (1) APEX KINGDOM, an unincorporated religious society and charitable
      trust having its principal office at [ADDRESS], Bridgeport,
      Connecticut (the "Kingdom"), acting by [NAME], [OFFICE]; and

  (2) [FULL LEGAL NAME OF SIGNER], of [RESIDENTIAL ADDRESS] (the
      "Member"),

each a "Party" and together the "Parties".

RECITALS

  A.  The Kingdom is a religious society and charitable trust
      constituted by its Charter dated 29 May 2025, which provides at
      Article II that membership is voluntary and that any member may
      withdraw at any time without penalty.

  B.  The Member is [a member of the Kingdom / a commissioned officer
      holding the office of [OFFICE] / an employee in the position of
      [POSITION] / a volunteer serving as [ROLE] / a contractor engaged
      to [DESCRIBE]].

  C.  The Parties share religious convictions concerning the resolution
      of disputes within the community of faith, and wish to have
      disputes between them determined in a forum applying the Kingdom's
      religious teaching, rather than in civil litigation.

  D.  No dispute has arisen between the Parties, and neither is aware of
      any circumstance likely to give rise to one. This agreement is made
      before the fact and for the future.

  E.  The Member has been given this document on [DATE], has had it for
      at least [SEVEN] days, has been advised in writing to consult a
      lawyer of the Member's own choosing before signing, and has been
      told in writing that declining to sign will have no adverse
      consequence of any kind.

THE PARTIES AGREE:


1.  CONSENT TO ECCLESIASTICAL JURISDICTION

1.1 The Member accepts the spiritual authority of the Kingdom and the
    jurisdiction of its ecclesiastical forums in matters of faith,
    doctrine, worship, membership, ordination, the holding of office
    within the Kingdom, and the internal discipline of members.

1.2 The Kingdom's ecclesiastical remedies are limited to admonition,
    counsel, suspension from office or from participation in rites,
    removal from office, and exclusion from fellowship. The Kingdom has
    no power to fine, to imprison, to seize property, to encumber any
    interest in property, or to compel the attendance of any person, and
    it claims none.

1.3 This Article 1 concerns religious governance only. It is not an
    agreement to arbitrate and creates no right enforceable in a civil
    court. A determination made under it binds the Member's standing
    within the Kingdom and nothing else.

1.4 The Member may withdraw from membership at any time, without penalty
    and without stating a reason, in accordance with Charter Article II.
    Withdrawal ends this Article 1 immediately.


2.  AGREEMENT TO ARBITRATE — SCOPE

2.1 Subject to Article 3, the Parties agree to submit to binding
    arbitration under this agreement any claim, dispute, or controversy
    between them, whether based in contract, tort, statute, equity, or
    the Kingdom's own law, arising out of or relating to:

    (a) the Member's membership in the Kingdom, its terms, its
        suspension, or its termination;

    (b) the Member's [office / employment / volunteer service /
        engagement] with the Kingdom, including its terms and its
        ending;

    (c) the internal governance, discipline, doctrine, polity, or
        administration of the Kingdom as it affects the Member;

    (d) any contribution, loan, or transfer of property made by the
        Member to the Kingdom or by the Kingdom to the Member;

    (e) any intellectual property created, contributed, or used by the
        Member in connection with the Kingdom; and

    (f) the following agreements between the Parties: [LIST BY TITLE AND
        DATE].

2.2 The agreement to arbitrate is mutual. The Kingdom is bound by it to
    the same extent as the Member, and the Kingdom may not bring in a
    civil court any claim it has agreed to arbitrate.

2.3 The Parties agree that this agreement affects commerce and is
    governed by the Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. § 1 et seq. To the
    extent the Federal Arbitration Act does not apply, the Parties agree
    that Connecticut's arbitration statute, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-408 et
    seq., governs.

2.4 [OPTIONAL — SEE THE NOTES BEFORE INCLUDING: Questions concerning the
    formation, validity, or scope of this agreement to arbitrate are for
    a court and not for the arbitrators.]


3.  MATTERS EXCLUDED — RIGHTS THAT ARE NOT WAIVED

3.1 Nothing in this agreement applies to, restricts, or waives any of the
    following, and any provision that purported to do so would be of no
    effect:

    (a) any criminal matter. Criminal jurisdiction belongs to the State
        of Connecticut and to the United States, and no agreement can
        transfer it or displace it;

    (b) the report of suspected abuse or neglect of a child to the
        Commissioner of Children and Families or to a law enforcement
        agency, and any duty of a mandated reporter under Conn. Gen.
        Stat. § 17a-101 et seq. No Party may be discouraged, delayed, or
        penalised for making such a report, and this agreement imposes
        no obligation of confidentiality with respect to one;

    (c) any matter concerning the custody, protection, safety, or
        welfare of a child, or any proceeding in which a child's
        interests are at issue;

    (d) any report to, communication with, charge filed with, complaint
        made to, or investigation or proceeding conducted by any
        government agency, including the Equal Employment Opportunity
        Commission, the Connecticut Commission on Human Rights and
        Opportunities, the National Labor Relations Board, the
        Occupational Safety and Health Administration, and the
        Connecticut Department of Labor;

    (e) any claim alleging conduct constituting sexual assault or sexual
        harassment, which the person making the claim may bring in court
        notwithstanding this agreement, as provided by 9 U.S.C.
        §§ 401–402;

    (f) any claim for benefits under the Workers' Compensation Act,
        Conn. Gen. Stat. chapter 568, or for unemployment compensation;

    (g) an application to a court for provisional or interim relief in
        aid of arbitration, or to compel arbitration, or to confirm,
        modify, or vacate an award; and

    (h) any other right or claim that as a matter of law may not be
        waived or submitted to arbitration by private agreement.

3.2 If any part of this agreement is held to conflict with clause 3.1, it
    is to be read as not applying to the excluded matter, and the
    remainder of the agreement continues in force.


4.  RULES AND SEAT

4.1 The arbitration is conducted under the [RULES OF THE ECCLESIASTICAL
    COURT OF APEX KINGDOM, rev. [N] ([DATE]), recorded in the Register of
    Instruments as [INST NUMBER]], a copy of which has been given to the
    Member with this agreement and forms part of it.

4.2 Where those rules are silent, the [RULES OF PROCEDURE FOR CHRISTIAN
    CONCILIATION / AMERICAN ARBITRATION ASSOCIATION COMMERCIAL
    ARBITRATION RULES] apply.

4.3 The seat of the arbitration is Bridgeport, Connecticut. Hearings may
    be held elsewhere or by remote means by agreement of the Parties or
    direction of the tribunal, without changing the seat.

4.4 The arbitration is conducted in English.

4.5 If the rules named in clause 4.1 are amended after the date of this
    agreement in a way that materially alters the procedure, the version
    given to the Member with this agreement continues to apply unless the
    Member agrees in writing to the amended version.


5.  THE TRIBUNAL

5.1 The tribunal consists of [three arbitrators / one arbitrator].

5.2 [WHERE THREE: Within twenty-one days of a written demand for
    arbitration, the Member nominates one arbitrator and the Kingdom
    nominates one arbitrator. The two so nominated jointly nominate the
    third, who presides. If they do not agree within twenty-one days of
    the second nomination, the third is appointed by [A NEUTRAL
    APPOINTING AUTHORITY NAMED HERE — e.g., the American Arbitration
    Association, or a named minister of a congregation unaffiliated with
    either Party].]

5.3 [WHERE ONE: The Parties jointly appoint a single arbitrator within
    twenty-one days of a written demand. If they do not agree, the
    arbitrator is appointed by [NEUTRAL APPOINTING AUTHORITY].]

5.4 An arbitrator must be a person of Christian faith in good standing
    with their congregation and must accept the religious character of
    the proceeding. Beyond that, no arbitrator need hold office in the
    Kingdom, and the Member may object to any nominee who does.

5.5 Every arbitrator must be, and must remain, independent and impartial,
    and must disclose in writing before accepting appointment any
    circumstance likely to give rise to justifiable doubt as to their
    impartiality or independence, including any relationship with either
    Party, any office held in the Kingdom, and any financial interest in
    the outcome. The duty of disclosure continues throughout.

5.6 Either Party may challenge an arbitrator for justifiable doubt as to
    impartiality or independence. A challenge is decided by [THE
    APPOINTING AUTHORITY NAMED IN CLAUSE 5.2], whose decision is final.

5.7 The Kingdom may not appoint, remove, instruct, or communicate ex
    parte with any arbitrator, and no officer of the Kingdom who has had
    any involvement in the subject matter of the dispute may sit.


6.  GOVERNING LAW

6.1 This agreement to arbitrate, its validity, and its enforcement are
    governed by the Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. § 1 et seq., and,
    so far as not inconsistent, by the law of the State of Connecticut.

6.2 In deciding the substance of a dispute the tribunal applies the
    Charter, the instruments and doctrine of the Kingdom, and the
    Kingdom's religious teaching, together with the law of the State of
    Connecticut so far as the Parties may lawfully agree that it applies
    and so far as it is not displaced by the foregoing.

6.3 An award may be entered as a judgment in any court having
    jurisdiction, as provided by 9 U.S.C. § 9. The Parties agree that a
    civil court asked to confirm an award need not, and should not,
    examine any question of religious doctrine in order to do so.


7.  COSTS

7.1 The Kingdom pays the fees and expenses of the arbitrators and all
    administrative costs of the forum, whatever the outcome, and whether
    the arbitration is commenced by the Kingdom or by the Member.

7.2 Each Party bears its own legal fees and the cost of its own
    witnesses, unless the tribunal orders otherwise on a ground provided
    by law or by the agreement out of which the dispute arises.

7.3 No Party may be required to pay any fee or cost as a condition of
    commencing or defending an arbitration under this agreement.


8.  CONFIDENTIALITY

8.1 The Parties will keep the proceedings and the award confidential,
    except so far as disclosure is required by law, is necessary to
    enforce or challenge the award, is made to a Party's own legal or
    financial advisers, or falls within Article 3.

8.2 Clause 8.1 does not apply to, and nothing in this agreement
    restricts, disclosure of conduct constituting sexual assault or
    sexual harassment, or the making of any report or complaint
    described in clauses 3.1(b), (c), or (d).


9.  THE MEMBER'S ACKNOWLEDGMENTS

The Member acknowledges that:

9.1 the Member has read this agreement, including the plain-language
    summary, and has had the opportunity to ask questions and to have
    them answered;

9.2 the Member received this document on [DATE], has had it in the
    Member's possession for at least [SEVEN] days, and was not asked to
    sign it on the day it was received;

9.3 the Member was advised in writing and orally to consult a lawyer of
    the Member's own choosing, at the Member's own expense, before
    signing, and [has done so / has chosen not to do so];

9.4 the Member was told, and understands, that declining to sign this
    agreement would have no consequence — no loss of membership, office,
    employment, assistance, participation, or standing of any kind;

9.5 the Member understands that by signing, the Member gives up the right
    to have the disputes described in Article 2 decided by a judge or a
    jury, and gives up the ordinary rights of appeal;

9.6 no dispute has arisen between the Parties as at the date of
    signature; and

9.7 the Member is eighteen years of age or older, is signing freely, and
    is not under any duress, undue influence, or promise not written in
    this document.


10. TERM, WITHDRAWAL, AND SURVIVAL

10.1 This agreement takes effect on the date of signature and continues
     until withdrawn.

10.2 Either Party may withdraw from Article 2 by written notice to the
     other. Withdrawal takes effect thirty days after the notice is
     received and operates only for the future.

10.3 A dispute submitted to arbitration before withdrawal takes effect
     remains subject to this agreement, as does any dispute arising out
     of events occurring before that date. Articles 3, 6, 7, and 8
     survive withdrawal.

10.4 Withdrawal from Article 2, and withdrawal from membership under
     clause 1.4, are separate acts. Neither requires the other.


11. GENERAL

11.1 If any provision of this agreement is held invalid or
     unenforceable, it is severed and the remainder continues in force,
     subject to clause 3.2.

11.2 This agreement, together with the rules incorporated by clause 4.1,
     is the entire agreement between the Parties on its subject matter,
     and replaces any earlier agreement or understanding about the
     resolution of disputes between them.

11.3 This agreement may be amended only in a writing signed by both
     Parties. A change to the Charter or to any instrument of the
     Kingdom does not amend it.

11.4 The Kingdom will deliver a signed copy of this agreement to the
     Member on the day of execution.

11.5 This agreement binds only the Member. It does not bind the Member's
     spouse, family, employer, congregation, heirs, or estate, and
     creates no obligation of any person who has not signed it.
```

## Notes

**Enforceability under the Federal Arbitration Act is the entire point of the
document.** Article 1 standing alone gives the Kingdom something real but
inward-facing: civil courts must abstain from resolving disputes over religious
doctrine, polity, and internal church governance — *Watson v. Jones*, 80 U.S. (13
Wall.) 679 (1871); *Serbian Eastern Orthodox Diocese v. Milivojevich*, 426 U.S.
696 (1976) — and the ministerial exception bars employment claims by those who
carry out religious functions, *Our Lady of Guadalupe School v. Morrissey-Berru*,
591 U.S. 732 (2020). Those doctrines keep a court out. They do not bring a court
in, and a determination of the Kingdom's tribunal, however carefully reached, is
not by itself something a civil court will enforce against anyone.

Article 2 is what changes that. Under 9 U.S.C. § 2 a written agreement to
arbitrate is valid, irrevocable, and enforceable save upon such grounds as exist
at law or in equity for the revocation of any contract; § 4 compels arbitration,
and § 9 provides for confirmation of an award as a judgment. Connecticut's own
arbitration statute, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-408 et seq., does the same work where
the federal Act does not reach, which is why clause 2.3 names both rather than
relying on the commerce requirement being satisfied — a membership covenant is not
obviously a contract evidencing a transaction involving commerce, and there is no
reason to bet the instrument on that question.

Religious arbitration sits squarely inside this framework. Courts confirm awards
from rabbinical courts and Christian conciliation panels without inquiring into
the doctrine applied, because what a court examines on a confirmation is the
agreement and the process, not the faith. Clause 6.3 says so expressly, which
costs nothing and orients the reader.

**How agreements of this kind fail.** Almost always for one of four reasons, and
every one of them is a drafting or a practice failure rather than bad luck.

*It was buried.* An arbitration clause in paragraph 34 of a membership handbook
nobody read is a clause a court will find was never assented to. This is why the
instrument stands alone, carries its own title, opens with a plain-language box,
and is not stapled to anything else.

*There was no genuine opportunity to decline.* Sign or lose the job, the
membership, the child's place, the assistance. This is procedural
unconscionability in its purest form, and it is the failure the Kingdom is most
exposed to, because a religious body holds things people need. Clause 9.4 and the
summary box state that declining costs nothing — and the statement is worthless
unless it is true. If anyone is ever treated worse for declining, every agreement
on this form is compromised, not just theirs.

*The terms were one-sided.* The classic markers: the institution may sue in court
while the signer may only arbitrate; the institution alone picks the panel; costs
are allocated so the signer cannot afford the forum they were pushed into.
Clause 2.2 makes the obligation mutual. Article 5 gives the Member a nomination,
a right of challenge, and a neutral appointing authority, and forbids the Kingdom
from appointing or instructing the tribunal. Article 7 puts the forum's costs on
the Kingdom whichever side commences — prohibitive costs are a recognised ground
for refusing to enforce (*Green Tree Financial Corp. v. Randolph*, 531 U.S. 79
(2000)), and the Kingdom gains nothing by economising here.

*It purported to waive the unwaivable.* This is the failure that does the most
damage, because a court that finds an agreement permeated by unlawful terms may
refuse to enforce the whole of it rather than blue-pencilling the offending
clause. Hence Article 3, which is longer than it needs to be on purpose. Note in
particular 9 U.S.C. §§ 401–402: since 2022, a person alleging conduct constituting
sexual assault or sexual harassment may elect to invalidate a pre-dispute
arbitration agreement as to that dispute, and no clause can take that election
away. The related point at clause 8.2 is the SPEAK OUT Act's treatment of
pre-dispute non-disclosure and non-disparagement terms in the same subject matter.
Any confidentiality clause that appeared to silence a person about sexual
misconduct, or to sit between a mandated reporter and Conn. Gen. Stat. § 17a-101,
would be worse than useless — it would be the exhibit.

**It must be signed before the dispute.** An agreement executed after a grievance
has formed is a submission to arbitration of that one dispute, not a general
consent, and it is construed narrowly against the party that drafted it. Worse,
its circumstances invite exactly the scrutiny the Kingdom wants to avoid: what did
the signer want, what did the Kingdom have, and what did they give up to get it.
Recital D and clause 9.6 fix the fact contemporaneously, which is why they are
there. This is also why the instrument should be circulated to the whole
membership now, in a calm month, rather than assembled as needed.

**The plain-language box.** It is not decoration and it is not a disclaimer. Its
function is evidentiary: it is what allows the Kingdom to show that this signer
knew what they were giving up. The two lines that matter most are the jury-trial
waiver and the statement that declining costs nothing, and both are stated in the
second person in ordinary words. The box says expressly that the articles govern
if the two ever differ, so that the summary cannot become a source of ambiguity
the Kingdom then has to litigate. Do not lengthen it. A summary that runs to two
pages has stopped being a summary and stopped doing this job.

**Clause 2.4, and why it is optional.** A clause delegating questions of
arbitrability to the arbitrators rather than the court is enforceable where the
delegation is clear and unmistakable (*Rent-A-Center, West, Inc. v. Jackson*, 561
U.S. 63 (2010)), and it is tactically attractive to an institution. It is
bracketed here in the opposite direction — reserving those questions to a court —
because for a body in the Kingdom's position the appearance of fairness is worth
more than the procedural advantage, and because a Kingdom-appointed tribunal ruling
on the validity of the Kingdom's own agreement is precisely the picture the
Kingdom does not want a judge to form. Take counsel's view before changing it.

**Article 1 and Article 2 are different instruments and should be recorded as
such.** The Register of Consents distinguishes a consent to ecclesiastical
jurisdiction from an arbitration agreement, and it does so because the two carry
different consequences: the first is strongly protected from civil review and
confers no civil enforceability; only the second produces an award a court will
confirm. Where a signer is offered only Article 1, record that, and do not let a
later summary describe the file as though everyone had signed an arbitration
agreement.

**The wet-ink original is the field the whole register exists to hold.** When
arbitration is resisted, the resisting party ordinarily denies signing. A produced
original bearing a witnessed and notarised signature ends that argument at the
threshold. A PDF of unknown provenance produces an evidentiary hearing the Kingdom
then has to win before it reaches anything else.

**Limits worth stating once.** Consent reaches only the person who gave it —
never their family, employer, congregation, or estate (clause 11.5). It creates no
authority over anyone else's property, no power over a non-signer, and no
jurisdiction over criminal conduct. Nothing issued under this agreement may be
styled as a summons, a warrant, a lien, a levy, or a judgment, and clause 1.2
states the outer limit of the Kingdom's remedies for the avoidance of any doubt.
Internal ecclesiastical discipline among people who agreed to it is legitimate and
protected; the same acts directed at someone who did not agree are not discipline,
they are torts, and several of them are crimes.

**Review it on a cycle.** Confirm every three years that the signer is still in
the capacity recorded, that the rules and forum still exist under the names used,
and that no intervening amendment has moved the agreement out from under them.
Where anything material has changed, take a fresh signature rather than argue that
the old one still reaches the new arrangement.

---

*This is an operating template prepared to organise the Kingdom's affairs. It is
not legal advice and no attorney-client relationship arises from it. Arbitration
agreements are among the most heavily litigated instruments in American law, the
rules governing them change, and enforceability turns on facts specific to each
signature. This instrument in particular should not be put into circulation until
licensed Connecticut counsel has reviewed it against the Kingdom's actual
practice.*
